newsitem.title: GUYANA: Guyana's president Jagan dies at 78 - Ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Guyana's president Jagan dies at 78 - Ambassador.

text.p: Guyana's president, Cheddi Jagan, died of apparent heart problems early on Thursday at Walter Reed military hospital in Washington, his wife and family by his side, Guyana's ambassador in Washington, Odeen Ishmael said. He was 78.
He had undergone heart surgery to clear a blocked artery after being taken to the United States for medical treatment Feb. 15, complaining of chest pains.
"The president is dead. The flame has now gone out," Ishmael told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.
Declaring six days of official mourning, Guyana's Prime Minister, Samuel Hinds, said in a statement: "His attending physician has certified that President Jagan died at 12:23 a.m. EST" (0523 GMT).
"That extraordinary light that shone in Guyana and the world for nearly 79 years has been extinguished," he said in the statement, read on radio and television.
"The greatest son and patriot that has ever walked this land has departed," he added.
Information Minister Moses Nagamootoo told Reuters that Hinds, who has been acting president since Jagan became ill, would be sworn in as president later on Thursday.
Hinds, 53, was expected to lead Guyana until national elections were held later this year or in early 1998.
Jagan's wife, two children and five grandchildren had rushed to his bedside to hold an all-night vigil, Ishmael said.
Jagan, a former Marxist, led his left-leaning People's Progressive Party (PPP) to a victory at the polls in October 1992 -- the country's first democratic elections in 28 years.
Under his leadership, Guyana enjoyed a relative economic boom. He embraced the free market system, admitting "there is no alternative" for his impoverished country.

The author of a wealth of books on Caribbean history, Jagan became Guyana's first prime minister after the former British colony was granted self-government in 1961, only to be deposed three years later after race riots.

Jagan was born on March 22, 1918 in Port Mourant, and qualified as a dentist in the United States, where he married Janet Rosenberg of Chicago, a relative of Ethel and Julius Rosenberg, who were executed in 1953 for espionage.
